findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage permission when the caller only has VIEW scope on all groups
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` checks `auth.groups().requireManage()`, any user granted only the `view` scope on the all-groups (`Groups`) resource will be allowed to create top-level groups and move existing child groups to the top level. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() in GroupPermissionsV2 never finds group resources and returns resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body:
There are three bugs in `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`:
1. It searches with `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`, but when individual group resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 121-128), `resource.setType(...)` is never called, so individual group resources have a `null` type. Only the all-groups resource (`Groups`) has type `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`.
2. Inside the callback it calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)`, but `hasPermission` looks up the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` where the resource's `name` is the group's ID, not the authorization resource's ID.
3. It adds `groupResource.getId()` (the authz resource UUID, or the `Groups` resource UUID) to `granted` instead of `groupResource.getName()` (the Keycloak group ID), which is then used to filter user group memberships in `UserModel.GROUPS`.

findings.title: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() does not handle GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE
findings.body: `getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` only resolves display names for `USERS` resources and falls back to `resource.getDisplayName()` otherwise. Because `getOrCreateResource` creates group resources with the group's UUID as the resource name and no display name, policies targeting `Groups` resources will have `null` (or raw UUIDs) as resource names when converted to representations instead of "All groups" or the group's name/path.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
findings.body: The Javadoc on `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` says `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` It should reference `{@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)}`.
